newsitem.title: USA: Fla. says Miss. tobacco deal won't slow its case.
newsitem.headline: Fla. says Miss. tobacco deal won't slow its case.

text.p: Florida will press ahead with its August 4 trial on its Medicaid lawsuit against the tobacco industry, despite an out-of-court settlement on a similar suit by Mississippi, a government spokesman said Thursday.
"There is no deal," said Joe Bizarro, spokesman for Florida Attorney General Bob Butterworth.
Florida is one of 40 state governments suing the tobacco industry to recover billions of dollars spent treating sick smokers in Medicaid healthcare programs.
Florida's $1 billion lawsuit is scheduled to go to trial Aug 4 in West Palm Beach. There are reports that Florida has been bargaining on a settlement, which would delay or eliminate a trial.

According to Bizarro, Mississippi Attorney General Mike Moore telephoned Butterworth late Wednesday night and outlined terms of his state's deal with cigarette makers. Mississippi had been scheduled to go to trial on Wednesday. It was to have been the first trial in any of the 40 Medicaid suits.
"Mississippi's settlement will have no effect on our plans to go to trial," Bizzaro said.
